Learning Objectives
By the end of this seminar, you will be able to:

Retrieve occurrence and environmental data programmatically in R
Process spatial datasets reproducibly with sf and terra
Quantify biodiversity using appropriate metrics
Model species distributions across environmental gradients

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text: Spatial Data: A Primer

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text:
What is Spatial Data?

Data that explicitly represents location on Earth’s surface, using coordinates within a defined reference system.



Vector (sf)

Points → occurrences
Lines → rivers, roads
Polygons → protected areas


Raster (terra)

Continuous gridded surfaces
Elevation, temperature, NDVI
Each cell = one value




Comprehensive treatment in1 and2.

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text:
Coordinate Reference Systems
The mathematical framework that links coordinates to locations on Earth.
\[
\text{CRS} = \{\,\text{datum},\ \text{projection},\ \text{units}\,\}
\]

# Always declare CRS explicitly with EPSG codes
st_crs(4326)   # WGS 84 — geographic, degrees
st_crs(3857)   # Web Mercator — projected, metres
st_crs(2100)   # GGRS87 / Greek Grid — projected, metres







Always check the CRS


Mismatched CRS is the #1 source of errors in spatial analysis.

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text:
Retrieving GBIF Data with R

library(rgbif)
library(sf)

# Search for Quercus ilex occurrences in Greece
occ <- occ_search(
  scientificName = "Quercus ilex",
  country        = "GR",
  hasCoordinate  = TRUE,
  limit          = 5000
)

# Convert to spatial object
pts <- st_as_sf(occ$data,
                coords = c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude"),
                crs    = 4326)

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text:
The sf Workflow

# Read country boundary
greece <- ne_countries(country = "Greece",
                       scale = "medium",
                       returnclass = "sf")

# Inspect
greece |> st_geometry() |> plot()

# Reproject
greece_2100 <- st_transform(greece, 2100)

# Compute area
greece_2100 |> st_area() |> units::set_units("km^2")

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text:
The terra Workflow

library(terra)
library(geodata)

# Download WorldClim bioclimatic variables (10 arc-min)
bioclim <- worldclim_global(var = "bio", res = 10, path = "data/raw")

# Crop to Greece extent
greece_ext <- ext(19, 30, 34, 42)
bio_gr <- crop(bioclim, greece_ext)

# Plot annual mean temperature (BIO1)
plot(bio_gr[[1]], main = "Annual Mean Temperature (°C)")

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text: Retrieving GBIF Occurrences

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text:
rgbif: Programmatic Access to GBIF

library(rgbif)

# 1. Resolve a taxon key
key <- name_backbone(name = "Quercus ilex")$usageKey

# 2. Search occurrences in Greece with valid coordinates
occ <- occ_search(
  taxonKey           = key,
  country            = "GR",
  hasCoordinate      = TRUE,
  hasGeospatialIssue = FALSE,
  limit              = 5000
)

# 3. Extract and convert to sf
pts <- occ$data |>
  select(species, decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude,
         year, basisOfRecord, datasetKey) |>
  drop_na(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude"),
           crs = 4326)

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text:
Visualising Raw Occurrences

ggplot() +
  annotation_map_tile(type = "cartolight", zoom = 6) +
  geom_sf(data = greece, fill = NA, color = "grey30") +
  geom_sf(data = pts, color = "#4A7C59", alpha = 0.5, size = 1) +
  labs(title    = expression(italic("Quercus ilex") ~ "occurrences in Greece"),
       subtitle = "Source: GBIF.org",
       caption  = "CRS: EPSG:4326") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

title: Day 1 — Spatial Data Retrieval & Analysis
text:
Cleaning with CoordinateCleaner

library(CoordinateCleaner)

flags <- clean_coordinates(
  x       = as.data.frame(occ$data),
  lon     = "decimalLongitude",
  lat     = "decimalLatitude",
  species = "species",
  tests   = c("capitals", "centroids", "equal",
              "gbif", "institutions", "zeros", "seas")
)

# Keep only records that pass all tests
clean <- occ$data[flags$.summary, ]







clean_coordinates() returns a logical matrix flagging each test individually — inspect failures before discarding!

p1 <- ggplot(greece) +

  geom_sf(data = pts_thin, color = "#4A7C59", alpha = 0.6, size = 0.8) +
  labs(title = paste("Thinned —", nrow(pts_thin), "records")) +

text:
Take-aways from Day 1

The R spatial stack (sf + terra) covers the full data pipeline
Always verify and harmonise CRS before any spatial operation
GBIF data are powerful but noisy — clean systematically
Document every step → reproducibility is non-negotiable

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text: Quantifying Biodiversity

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
The α, β, γ Framework
Following1:
\[
\gamma = \alpha \times \beta
\]



Component
Scale
R function




α (alpha)
Local richness
vegan::specnumber()


β (beta)
Turnover among sites
betapart::beta.pair()


γ (gamma)
Regional richness
vegan::specpool()

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
Hill Numbers — A Unified Framework
\[
{}^{q}\!D = \left( \sum_{i=1}^{S} p_i^{\,q} \right)^{1/(1-q)}
\]

(q = 0): species richness
(q = 1): exponential of Shannon entropy
(q = 2): inverse Simpson concentration


library(iNEXT)
out <- iNEXT(community_data, q = c(0, 1, 2),
             datatype = "abundance", endpoint = 500)
ggiNEXT(out, type = 1) + scale_color_viridis_d(option = "D")

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
α-Diversity Example

library(vegan)
data(BCI)   # tropical tree community

div <- tibble(
  site     = rownames(BCI),
  S        = specnumber(BCI),
  H        = diversity(BCI, index = "shannon"),
  Simpson  = diversity(BCI, index = "simpson"),
  Pielou_J = H / log(S)
)

div |>
  pivot_longer(-site) |>
  ggplot(aes(value)) +
  geom_histogram(fill = "#4A7C59", bins = 20) +
  facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free")

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
β-Diversity: Turnover vs Nestedness
2 decomposed Sørensen β into two components:
\[
\beta_{\text{SOR}} = \beta_{\text{SIM}} + \beta_{\text{SNE}}
\]

library(betapart)

# Convert abundance to presence/absence
pa <- ifelse(BCI > 0, 1, 0)

# Pairwise multi-component beta
bp <- beta.pair(pa, index.family = "sorensen")

# Mean values
sapply(bp, mean)
#>  beta.sim  beta.sne  beta.sor
#>      0.41      0.06      0.47

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
Visualising β-Diversity

library(ape)

# UPGMA on turnover
hc <- hclust(bp$beta.sim, method = "average")

# NMDS ordination
nmds <- metaMDS(bp$beta.sor, k = 2, trymax = 50)

plot(nmds, type = "t", main = "NMDS — Sørensen dissimilarity")

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
Predictor Selection — Multicollinearity

library(usdm)

# Variance Inflation Factor stepwise selection
v <- vifstep(bio_gr, th = 5)
v
#> 4 variables from 19 input variables have collinearity problem:
#>   bio6 bio11 bio16 bio17

# Keep only retained predictors
preds <- bio_gr[[v@results$Variables]]







A VIF threshold of 5–10 is common; lower is stricter.

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
Background / Pseudo-absences

library(predicts)

# 10,000 random background points within Greece
set.seed(42)
bg <- spatSample(preds, size = 10000,
                 method = "random", na.rm = TRUE,
                 as.points = TRUE, values = FALSE)

# Extract environmental values at presence + background
pres_env <- extract(preds, vect(pts_thin))
bg_env   <- extract(preds, bg)

train <- bind_rows(
  mutate(pres_env, occ = 1),
  mutate(as_tibble(bg_env), occ = 0)
) |> drop_na()

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
Fitting a MaxEnt-style Model

library(predicts)

# MaxEnt via the `predicts` package (successor of `dismo`)
mod <- MaxEnt(
  x = preds,
  p = st_coordinates(pts_thin),
  removeDuplicates = TRUE
)

# Predict habitat suitability
suit <- predict(preds, mod, type = "cloglog")
plot(suit, col = viridis(100), main = "Habitat suitability")

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
Spatial Block Cross-Validation

library(blockCV)

sb <- cv_spatial(
  x         = pts_thin,
  column    = "occ",
  k         = 5,
  size      = 50000,   # 50 km blocks
  selection = "random",
  iteration = 100
)

cv_plot(cv = sb, x = pts_thin)







Random CV inflates SDM performance by exploiting spatial autocorrelation. Always use spatial blocking for honest evaluation.

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
Model Evaluation

library(predicts)

eval_metrics <- pa_evaluate(
  p = predict(mod, pres_env_test),
  a = predict(mod, bg_env_test)
)

eval_metrics
#>   AUC    : 0.87
#>   COR    : 0.42
#>   max TSS: 0.61

text: Biogeographical Regionalisation

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
From β-Diversity to Bioregions
The workflow:

Build a site × species matrix on a regular grid
Compute pairwise β-diversity (betapart)
Apply hierarchical clustering (hclust)
Cut the dendrogram → bioregions
Map back to space



See3 and4 for ecoregion delineation methods.

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
Mapping Bioregions

grid_clust <- grid |>
  filter(cell_id %in% rownames(mat)) |>
  mutate(region = factor(clusters))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = greece, fill = "grey95") +
  geom_sf(data = grid_clust, aes(fill = region),
          color = NA, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", name = "Bioregion") +
  labs(title    = "Biogeographical regionalisation of Greece",
       subtitle = "Based on Simpson β-diversity (turnover)",
       caption  = "Data: GBIF · CRS: EPSG:4326") +
  theme_void()

title: Day 2 — Biodiversity & Biogeographical Patterns
text:
Synthesis & Take-aways

R offers a complete, reproducible pipeline for spatial ecology
Choose biodiversity metrics that match your question, not vice-versa
SDMs are powerful but require honest evaluation (spatial CV)
Biogeographical patterns emerge from β-diversity structure
Document, version, share → open science is good science
